_notice: SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION DATA. Illustrative process and ranges for a fictional agency. Not a real fee schedule.
_policy: Ranges here are deliberately WIDE and are returned as ranges with their drivers attached. There is no single-number field anywhere in this file, so an agent has nothing to quote from even if it tries. See BRIEF 2f.

steps: Ingredient and supplier review — every ingredient traced to its own certification.
Plant inspection by a rabbinic coordinator.
Determination of mashgiach requirement — visits, or full-time presence, depending on what is produced.
Contract, fee schedule, and certification issued.
Ongoing: scheduled and unannounced inspections, annual renewal.
timelineDrivers: how quickly the ingredient list can be verified with upstream suppliers
whether any ingredient needs its own certification obtained first
how much equipment kashering the changeover requires

costDrivers: number of distinct products and production lines
ingredient complexity and how many suppliers need upstream verification
mashgiach hours — periodic visits versus full-time presence on site
whether equipment kashering or line dedication is required

annualRangeUsd._comment: Order-of-magnitude bands only, always delivered as a band with drivers. Never as a figure.

simple.describes: single facility, few products, all ingredients already certified, periodic mashgiach visits

moderate.describes: single or dual facility, a dozen or more products, some upstream verification needed

complex.describes: multiple facilities, extensive product range, full-time mashgiach, or significant kashering

faq.q: Do we certify a single product or the whole company?
faq.a: Either. Many companies start with one line and expand the certification later.

faq.q: Does the company need a full-time mashgiach?
faq.a: It depends entirely on what is produced. Many facilities need only periodic visits; meat, cooked foods, and some dairy operations need full-time presence.

faq.q: Can certification be backdated to cover stock already produced?
faq.a: No. Certification covers production under supervision from the date it is issued.
